question: Will Ukraine strike a Russian oil refinery between October 29 and October 31, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Base rate: during active campaign phases (Sep-Oct 2026) Ukraine produced refinery hits every few days, implying ~60-75% for any 3-day window. Since the Oct 15 Ryazan strike, strikes have shifted toward terminals/depots/pipelines (St Petersburg oil terminal & Ruchi depot Oct 18-19, Tambov Nikolskoye pumping station Oct 20) with no clearly confirmed refinery hit Oct 16-22, while US pressure is intense (reported intelligence-sharing threats, Starlink throttling, Patriot shortage) and Zelensky publicly offered a 30-day refinery-strike pause for Patriots, which US reportedly rebuffed. Massive drone volume continues (373 drones Oct 21), and loose media labeling of terminals as 'refineries' adds some YES tail. No matching human market found (Manifold 'strike Russia sovereign land before December' at 0.75 is far broader).
calls.dossier:
- Oct 8-9 2026: Ukraine hit Omsk refinery (FP-6 drones) and Ukhta refinery (An-196, ~1,900 km) (Ukrainska Pravda, Oct 9).
- Oct 11: Trump announced 'energy ceasefire'; Ukraine paused energy strikes ~3 days (Axios/NBC).
- Oct 15: Zelensky declared Kyiv 'done' with truce; Ryazan refinery hit, CDU-6 halted (Kyiv Independent/Reuters, Oct 17). Trump called it 'a disgrace' (Al Jazeera Oct 15).
- Oct 16: industrial facility fire in Surgut region after drone attack (Kyiv Independent tag page).
- Oct 18-19: >1,000-drone attack on Russia; St Petersburg Oil Terminal and Ruchi oil depot hit (Al Jazeera, Kyiv Independent). France24/Channels TV loosely described 'two refineries ablaze' in St Petersburg; Al Jazeera/KI describe terminal/depot, not refinery.
- Oct 20: Nikolskoye pumping station (Druzhba pipeline), Tambov Oblast, fire confirmed by governor (Moscow Times/Euromaidan, Oct 20) - non-refinery.
- Oct 21 night: Russia MoD claimed record 373 Ukrainian drones downed over 14 regions; no refinery damage found in reports (AiF, Fontanka).
- Searched and found no clearly confirmed refinery hit Oct 16-22.
- Oct 19: Zelensky told US senators Patriots nearly exhausted; offered 30-day halt of refinery strikes in exchange for Patriot interceptors; US envoys reportedly showed no openness (Kyiv Post, Euromaidan Oct 20). Zelensky said US warned of cutting intel sharing if refinery campaign continued; Rubio said 'no pause'.
- Background: Ukraine hit 12 Russian refineries in September 2026 (Euromaidan); defense ministry claims 51% of capacity disabled.
- Status quo: campaign active against oil infrastructure broadly; refinery-specific hits since Oct 15 sparse; US pressure ongoing; possible pause deal is the key regime-break candidate toward NO; continued massed drone raids are the candidate toward YES.
- Base rate: during active phases (Sep-early Oct 2026) refinery hits came every few days (~12 refineries in Sep => roughly 3-4 per 10 days); post-Oct-15 rate ~1 confirmed refinery hit per 7 days.
- Resolution instrument: resolves off General Staff, Russian regional officials, or credible media reporting impact/fire/damage at a crude refinery in pre-2014 Russia; terminals, depots, pumping stations do not count; preponderance rule if conflicting.
- Event window: Oct 29 00:00 -> Oct 31 24:00 Moscow time per criteria; as of Oct 22 0% elapsed (window starts in ~7 days).
- Searched but not found: any Polymarket/Kalshi contract on refinery strikes in this window (none found); any agreed new truce as of Oct 22.

calls.reasoning: Base rate: during the active campaign (Sept to early Oct 2026, about 12 refineries hit in September), a 3-day window almost always had a refinery hit, around 85%. Regime change: after the Oct 15 Ryazan hit I found no confirmed refinery hit Oct 16-21. Ukraine's strikes moved to an oil terminal and depot around St Petersburg (Oct 18-19) and a Druzhba pumping station (Oct 20), consistent with avoiding refineries specifically under US pressure (intelligence-cutoff threats, Kushner at Oslo on Oct 20). Zelensky said Ukraine would halt refinery strikes if Russia reciprocated, and Witkoff was due to take a proposal to Putin on Oct 21, so a reciprocal energy truce before Oct 29 is plausible. Counterpoints: the earlier truce collapsed within days, Russia keeps hitting Ukrainian energy, and Ukraine has already defied Trump once. A post-Oct 15 rate of about 1 hit/week gives roughly 35% for 3 days; weighed against escalation and truce scenarios, 40%. Market check: no matching market found; the Manifold 'strike Russia sovereign land before December' (0.75) is a far broader contract and is not used as an anchor.

Zelensky said Ukraine is ready to refrain from striking 'sensitive parts' of Russia's energy sector if Moscow stops hitting Ukrainian energy. No formal agreement; the US cited 'meaningful progress' (Ukrainska Pravda / Axios, Oct 21).
- Witkoff was scheduled to present an updated peace proposal to Putin in St Petersburg on Oct 21; a possible trilateral meeting is mentioned. Outcome not found.
- Zelensky earlier offered a 30-day refinery-strike halt in exchange for Patriot interceptors; US envoys reportedly showed no openness (Euromaidan, Oct 20).
- Russia continued striking Ukrainian energy: Zelensky counted 76 attacks in the week after Oct 11 (Al Jazeera, Oct 19).
- Status quo: Ukraine is formally not under any truce, but its strikes since Oct 15 have hit only non-refinery oil infrastructure as far as found.
- Base-rate components: active-campaign regime (Sept to early Oct 2026) had roughly 0.4-0.6 refinery hits/day, so 3-day windows almost always contained one. Post-Oct-15 regime: 1 refinery hit in about 7 days (Oct 15 itself). Truce regime (Oct 11-14): 0 in 3 days.
- Searched but not found: any refinery hit Oct 16-22; the outcome of the Witkoff-Putin meeting; any human prediction market on this exact question.

calls.reasoning: Status quo: Ukraine's refinery campaign has been active since Zelensky ended the Trump 'energy ceasefire' on Oct 15. Confirmed refinery hits include Omsk Oct 8, Ukhta Oct 9 and Ryazan Oct 15; St Petersburg Oct 18 was mostly a terminal and depot. During active phases, qualifying refinery hits come every ~1-3 days, so a 3-day window is hit roughly 75-85% of the time. The main downside is a renewed mutual energy truce. US pressure is heavy before the Nov 3 midterms (Kushner in Oslo Oct 20, Witkoff met Putin Oct 21), Zelensky offered on Oct 20 to stop if Russia stops, and trilateral talks are floated for early November. I give ~20% to a pause covering Oct 29-31. Some raids also hit only depots or terminals, or are fully intercepted. No matching human market was found; the Manifold 'strike Russia sovereign land before December' market (0.75) is a far broader near-miss and was not used as an anchor.

calls.reasoning: Active-campaign base rate (Sept-early Oct 2026, ~12 refineries/month) implies ~75-85% for a 3-day window, but since the Oct 15 Ryazan hit no confirmed refinery hit was found Oct 16-22; Ukraine's strikes shifted to terminals, depots, a pumping station and an unclear Surgut energy plant, consistent with managing heavy US pressure before the Nov 3 midterms. No mutual truce is agreed (Witkoff-Putin Oct 21 produced only technical talks next month), the previous pause collapsed in 3 days, and massed raids continue, keeping YES live. Zelensky's offer of a 30-day refinery pause for Patriots is a NO tail. Current-regime rate ~1 refinery hit/week gives ~35-40%; adding escalation risk, loose 'refinery' labeling and the debris clause lifts it to ~47%. calls.reconciliation: Runs split 0.40/0.55/0.68 mainly on which regime will hold: September's high tempo or the slower post-Oct-15 pace. Checks: (1) refinery hits Oct 16-22: searches found none confirmed; Oct 18 St Petersburg was a terminal and depot, and the Oct 16 Surgut 'energy plant' type is unclear (an unconfirmed Kyiv Post Rostov oil-terminal item is non-refinery anyway). This supports runs 1-2 on the current pace. (2) Witkoff-Putin Oct 21 outcome: Russia agreed only to resume technical talks next month, with no energy truce; Putin's 'simply ridiculous' rejection dates from Oct 2 Valdai. This lowers the chance of a mutual truce, which weakens run 2's truce scenario. (3) Ukraine pause decision as of Oct 22: no new pause announced; the 30-day pause-for-Patriots offer is still pending, and the US denies threatening intelligence cuts. Remaining dispute is judgment: whether the shift away from refineries is deliberate restraint or chance. I take it as partial restraint, so I land below run 1 and above run 2.
